9324-roden-s-corner.creator: Henry Seton Merriman
9324-roden-s-corner.description: A book by Henry Seton Merriman. During the daytime the passer-by will, if he looks up quickly enough, see furtive faces at the windows, of men, and more especially of women, who never seem to come abroad, but pass their lives behind those unwashed curtains, with carefully closed windows, and in an atmosphere which may be faintly imagined by a glance at the wares in the shop below.

arxiv-2107-08900.title: Parametric estimation for functional autoregressive processes on the sphere
arxiv-2107-08900.creator: Alessia Caponera, Claudio Durastanti
arxiv-2107-08900.description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to define a nonlinear least squares estimator for the spectral parameters of a spherical autoregressive process of order 1 in a parametric setting. Furthermore, we investigate on its asymptotic properties, such as weak consistency and asymptotic normality. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 60G60, 62G05; Secondary 62R30 60G10 1.

arxiv-2208-07534.creator: Tatsuo Nishitani
arxiv-2208-07534.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tatsuo Nishitani. In this note, we improve a previously proven non-solvability result of the Cauchy problem in the Gevrey class for a homogeneous second-order differential operator mentioned in the title. We prove that the Cauchy problem for this operator is not locally solvable at the origin for any lower order term in the Gevrey class of order greater than 5 5 , lowering the previously obtained Gevrey order 6 6 .

arxiv-2305-03390.title: Evidence that PUBO outperforms QUBO when solving continuous optimization problems with the QAOA DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference Companion (GECCO’23 Companion); July 15–19, 2023; Lisbon, Portugal Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference
arxiv-2305-03390.creator: Jonas Stein, Farbod Chamanian, Maximilian Zorn, Jonas Nüßlein, Sebastian Zielinski, Michael Kölle, Claudia Linnhoff-Popien
arxiv-2305-03390.description: Abstract . Quantum computing provides powerful algorithmic tools that have been shown to outperform established classical solvers in specific optimization tasks. A core step in solving optimization problems with known quantum algorithms such as the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is the problem formulation.

arxiv-2307-02085.title: Finite period vectors and Gauss sums
arxiv-2307-02085.creator: Yeongseong Jo
arxiv-2307-02085.description: Abstract . We study four sums including the Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika, Flicker, Bump–Friedberg, and Jacquet–Shalika sums associated to irreducible cuspidal representations of general linear groups over finite fields. By computing explicitly, we relate Asai and Bump–Friedberg gamma factors over finite fields to those over nonarchimedean local fields through level zero supercuspidal representation.

arxiv-2407-06279.title: Wigner’s friend scenarios: on what to condition and how to verify the predictions
arxiv-2407-06279.creator: Flavio Del Santo, Gonzalo Manzano, Časlav Brukner
arxiv-2407-06279.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Flavio Del Santo, Gonzalo Manzano, Časlav Brukner. Wigner’s friend experiment and its modern extensions display the ambiguity of the quantum mechanical description regarding the assignment of quantum states. While the friend applies the state-update rule to the system upon observing an outcome of her measurement in a quantum system, Wigner describes the friend’s measurement as a unitary evolution, resulting in an entangled state for the composite system of the friend and the system.

arxiv-2502-13772.title: Quantile agent utility and implications to randomized social choice
arxiv-2502-13772.creator: Ioannis Caragiannis, Sanjukta Roy
arxiv-2502-13772.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ioannis Caragiannis, Sanjukta Roy. We initiate a novel direction in randomized social choice by proposing a new definition of agent utility for randomized outcomes. Each agent has a preference over all outcomes and a quantile parameter. Given a lottery over the outcomes, an agent gets utility from a particular representative , defined as the least preferred outcome that can be realized so that the probability that any worse-ranked outcome can be realized is at most the agent’s quantile value.

arxiv-2508-09812.title: Poaching Hotspot Identification Using Satellite Imagery
arxiv-2508-09812.creator: \IEEEauthorblockN Aryan Pandhi (ap663), Shrey Baid (sb857), Sanjali Jha (sj373)
arxiv-2508-09812.description: Abstract 1 Motivation Elephant Poaching in African countries has been a decade-old problem. So much so that African Forest Elephants are now listed as an endangered species, and African Savannah Elephants as critically endangered by the IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature).

arxiv-2512-00568.creator: Alejandro De Las Peñas Castaño
arxiv-2512-00568.description: Abstract . For a product E 1 × E 2 E_{1}\times E_{2} of two elliptic curves over a p p -adic field with good supersingular reduction, we produce infinitely many rational equivalences in the Chow group CH 0 ​ ( X ) \mathrm{CH}_{0}(X) of zero cycles via genus 2 covers of E 1 E_{1} and E 2 E_{2} .

arxiv-2512-17991.title: Recasting Schrödinger’s Cat Thought Experiment as a Remote Measurement Problem
arxiv-2512-17991.creator: Lucas L. Brugger, Cristhiano Duarte, Bruno F. Rizzuti
arxiv-2512-17991.description: Abstract With 2025 being declared the Year of Quantum Science and Technology, our contribution seeks to provide a fresh perspective on Schrödinger’s cat thought experiment. We reinterpret this experiment by viewing it through the lens of quantum theory as a generalisation of classical probability, rooted in a Bayesian subjectivist framework.

arxiv-2512-21316.title: Scaling Laws for Economic Productivity: Experimental Evidence in LLM-Assisted Consulting, Data Analyst, and Management Tasks Thanks: I gratefully acknowledge financial support from Coefficient Giving to conduct this research. The research described in this article was approved by the Yale Human Rese
arxiv-2512-21316.creator: Ali Merali
arxiv-2512-21316.description: Abstract This paper derives “Scaling Laws for Economic Impacts”- empirical relationships between the training compute of Large Language Models (LLMs) and professional productivity. In a preregistered experiment, over 500 consultants, data analysts, and managers completed professional tasks using one of 13 LLMs.

arxiv-2602-19359.title: Vid2Sid : Videos Can Help Close the Sim2Real Gap
arxiv-2602-19359.creator: Kevin Qiu 1,2 , Yu Zhang 3 , Marek Cygan 1,4 , Josie Hughes 3
arxiv-2602-19359.description: Abstract Calibrating a robot simulator’s physics parameters (friction, damping, material stiffness) to match real hardware is often done by hand or with black-box optimizers that reduce error but cannot explain which physical discrepancies drive the error. When sensing is limited to external cameras, the problem is further compounded by perception noise and the absence of direct force or state measurements.

pmc-10507027.title: Validation of deep learning-based CT image reconstruction for treatment planning
pmc-10507027.creator: Keisuke Yasui, Yasunori Saito, Azumi Ito, Momoka Douwaki, Shuta Ogawa, Yuri Kasugai, Hiromu Ooe, Yuya Nagake, Naoki Hayashi
pmc-10507027.description: Deep learning-based CT image reconstruction (DLR) is a state-of-the-art method for obtaining CT images. This study aimed to evaluate the usefulness of DLR in radiotherapy. Data were acquired using a large-bore CT system and an electron density phantom for radiotherapy.

pmc-10684621.title: Pharmacokinetics and Tolerability of Zibotentan in Patients with Concurrent Moderate Renal and Moderate Hepatic Impairment
pmc-10684621.creator: Anne-Kristina Mercier, Mikael Sunnåker, Sebastian Ueckert, Tadeusz Pawlik, Emilia Henricson, Oleksandr Molodetskyi, Gordon C. Law, Victoria E. R. Parker, Jan Oscarsson
pmc-10684621.description: Background and ObjectiveZibotentan, a selective endothelin A receptor antagonist, is in development for chronic liver and kidney disease. The pharmacokinetics (PK) of zibotentan were previously investigated in patients with either renal impairment or hepatic impairment, but the impact of both pathologies on PK was not evaluated.

Meanwhile, Candida tropicalis is an unconventional diploid yeast, most significantly characterized by its ability to metabolize alkanes or fatty acids for growth and proliferation. Therefore, perillic acid’s precursor (L-limonene) in C.

pmc-11657350.title: Healthcare utilisation patterns and contributory factors among middle-aged adults: a scoping review
pmc-11657350.creator: Yong Ng, Abigail Jia Ai Low, Clement Chan, Yu Liang Lim, Chien Earn Lee, Hiang Khoon Tan, Qin Xiang Ng
pmc-11657350.description: BackgroundMiddle-aged adults, defined as individuals between the ages of 45 and 64, represent a significant yet under researched group of healthcare service users. This scoping review aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of the patterns of healthcare utilisation and the factors contributing to them within this demographic.

pmc-12442340.title: The persistent effects of exposure to a predator odor stressor on sensitivity to alcohol
pmc-12442340.creator: Ryan E. Tyler, Maya N. Bluitt, Kalynn J. Van Voorhies, Wen Liu, Sarah N. Magee, Elisabeth R. Pitrolo, Victoria L. Cordero, Laura C. Ornelas, Caroline G. Krieman, Brooke N. Bender, Alejandro M. Mosera, Joyce Besheer
pmc-12442340.description: Traumatic stress is linked to problematic alcohol use, yet its persistent effects on alcohol sensitivity remain unclear. This study examined the long-term effects of traumatic stress on alcohol sensitivity in male and female Long-Evans rats. Rats were trained to discriminate alcohol (2 g/kg, i.g.

pmc-12525410.title: Comparison of Aerosol Generation Between Bag Valve and Chest Compression-Synchronized Ventilation During Simulated Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
pmc-12525410.creator: Young Taeck Oh, Choung Ah Lee, Daun Choi, Hang A. Park
pmc-12525410.description: Background: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation can generate aerosols, potentially exposing healthcare workers (HCWs) to infection. Bag valve ventilation (BV) is widely used but is prone to aerosol dispersion, whereas chest compression-synchronized ventilation (CCSV) maintains a closed respiratory circuit. In this study, we compared aerosol generation between CCSV and BV during chest compressions following endotracheal intubation in a simulated resuscitation setting.

pmc-12586710.title: Myoblast paracrine factors induce catabolic remodelling in electrically stimulated myotubes
pmc-12586710.creator: Magda A. Lesinski, Michael J. Kamal, Gianni Parise
pmc-12586710.description: Skeletal muscle plasticity is strongly influenced by a multitude of cell populations within the muscle niche. Satellite cells, or resident muscle stem cells, play an essential role in skeletal muscle remodelling after injury where they differentiate into myoblasts and directly donate myonuclei to damaged fibres thereby promoting protein synthesis.

pmc-12589504.title: Deep reinforcement learning-based intrusion detection scheme for software-defined networking
pmc-12589504.creator: R. Kanimozhi, P. S. Ramesh
pmc-12589504.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). A robust Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Intrusion Detection Scheme (DRL-IDS) for Software-Defined Networking (SDN) which combines the Long-Short Term Sequence Recurrent Neural Network (LFTS-RNN) with the Particle Cloud-Integrated Joint Time- and Feature-Optimization Algorithm (PC-JTFOA). The hybrid model aims to enhance the security of SDN through the detection and mitigation of a wide array of Distributed Denial of Service attacks and network misbehaviors across different SDN planes. The LFTS-RNN is used for accurate attack detection and misbehavior identification.

pmc-12748189.title: Identification of QTLs for internode length and diameter associated with lodging resistance in rice
pmc-12748189.creator: Qiuyun Lin, Ping Gan, Yujie Zhou, Yuehui Lin, Zhenyu Xie, Wei Hu
pmc-12748189.description: IntroductionLodging is a significant challenge in rice production, particularly for high-yielding cultivars. Previous research has shown that stem characteristics, such as internode length and diameter, are key determinants of lodging resistance. However, the genetic mechanisms controlling these traits remain poorly understood.

pmc-13027865.title: Remimazolam Bolus Prevents Emergence Agitation After Rhinologic Surgery: A Randomized, Triple-Blind, Controlled Trial
pmc-13027865.creator: Grgur Prižmić, Filip Periš, Marinela Jozeljić Pešić, Ana Maria Mitar, Ana Bego, Sanja Pavičić Perković, Sanda Stojanović Stipić
pmc-13027865.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Emergence agitation (EA) is common after rhinologic surgery and may cause self-injury, bleeding, and prolonged post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine that may reduce EA without delaying recovery. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of a single dose of remimazolam administered at the end of surgery on the incidence of EA in adult patients undergoing nasal surgery.

pmc-13078876.title: Diet’s rapid effects on the thyroid gland challenge unidirectional assumptions about hypothyroidism and energy balance
pmc-13078876.creator: Arturo Hernandez, Francesco S Celi
pmc-13078876.description: Thyroid hormones provide crucial regulation of energy expenditure through their effects on thermogenesis, lipid metabolism, and mitochondrial function. Given their close relationship with overall metabolism, a deficit in thyroid hormones fittingly leads to a positive energy balance and weight gain. The direction of this process may also operate in reverse, according to recent research from Rampy et al.

pmc-13198370.title: An oncologic cardiotoxicity masquerading as ST-elevated myocardial infarction: a case report
pmc-13198370.creator: Amarpal Karamjit Singh, Rifly Rafiudeen, Chiew Wong
pmc-13198370.description: BackgroundFluoropyrimidines, such as 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), when used in combination with bevacizumab are associated with diverse cardiotoxic effects, including vasospasm, myocarditis, and myopericarditis. These toxicities may closely mimic acute coronary syndrome, creating diagnostic uncertainty and risk of inappropriate management. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is central in distinguishing inflammatory myocardial injury from ischaemic pathology.

pmc-13282927.title: Modified Sick Neonatal Score in Predicting Outcomes of Neonates Admitted to the NICU at a Tertiary Care Center in Northern India
pmc-13282927.creator: Goud Priyanka, Ekansh Rathoria, Mridula Srivastava, Utkarsh Bansal, Prerna Priyadarshini, Rohitash Lahari, Richa Rathoria
pmc-13282927.description: BackgroundEarly identification of critically ill neonates is essential for timely intervention and improved outcomes, particularly in resource-limited settings. Several neonatal illness severity scoring systems have been developed to predict mortality; however, many rely on laboratory investigations and complex calculations, limiting their applicability in low-resource health care settings.

pmc-13486226.title: Uniaxial Stress Enhanced Anisotropic Magnetoresistance and Superconductivity in the Kagome Superconductor LaRu3Si2
pmc-13486226.creator: P Kral, V Sazgari, Y Ge, O Gerguri, M Spitaler, JN Graham, H Nakamura, M Bartkowiak, S Nakatsuji, H Luetkens, G Simutis, G Xu, Z Guguchia
pmc-13486226.description: To elucidate how kagome electronic structure governs quantum ground states, we introduce a unique approach combining in‐plane uniaxial stress tuning, magnetotransport, and first‐principles calculations to uncover its impact on superconducting and normal‐state properties in LaRu3Si2. We identify a pronounced anisotropy in both the upper critical field and the normal‐state magnetoresistance, indicating strong electronic anisotropy despite the three‐dimensional crystal structure.

pmc-13533023.title: Exploring the Role of Metabolites in Torsadogenic Risk Assessment: A Text-Mining Approach
pmc-13533023.creator: Egemen BİLGİN, Gülçin TUĞCU, Ahmet AYDIN
pmc-13533023.description: ObjectivesTorsades de pointes (TdP) is a life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia often caused by the inadvertent inhibition of the human ether-à-go-go-related gene (hERG). Conventional pre-market evaluations, which emphasize parent molecules, often yield inaccurate predictions due to the multifaceted nature of TdP. This study aimed to investigate the role of metabolites and their interplay with parent molecules in the manifestation of TdP.

pmc-13547697.title: Gate‐Tunable Polarity‐Reconfigurable Photovoltaic Response With Dual Linearity in NbS3/WSe2 Heterostructures for In‐Sensor Image Processing
pmc-13547697.creator: Jidong Liu, Jianxiong Xie, Qiaoyan Hao, Yutao Hu, Zhen He, Haolin Liu, Danting Lin, Haibo Gan, Yudi Tu, Wenjing Zhang
pmc-13547697.description: Reconfigurable optoelectronic image sensors capable of in‐sensor computing are promising for energy‐efficient edge visual perception. Self‐powered photovoltaic operation further reduces the power demand of image sensing and processing. However, it remains challenging to achieve a continuously gate‐tunable self‐powered photovoltaic response that combines reversible polarity with linear weight programmability.

pmc-13647533.title: University students’ contribution to advancing malaria eradication efforts in Rwanda
pmc-13647533.creator: Olivier Abayisenga, Darius Benimana, Pierre Clever Byishimo, Aline Niyigena, Gilbert Nizeyimana, Solive Jovise Umuhire, Joshua Kwizera, Iradukunda Daniel, Jerome Mfitumukiza, Olivier Uwishema
pmc-13647533.description: BackgroundMalaria is a life-threatening disease caused and spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes. It is a global health concern, especially in tropical areas, where the WHO Africa region published 94% of malaria cases and 95% of deaths related to malaria in children under 5 years old. In Rwanda, malaria continues to affect the population, where rural communities are at risk.

pmc-13654887.title: Reversed sound–shape association in tortoises (Testudo marginata)
pmc-13654887.creator: Giovanna Marliani, Gionata Stancher, Maria Loconsole
pmc-13654887.description: Crossmodal correspondences, spontaneous links between sensory modalities, are well documented in humans and other animals. The Bouba–Kiki effect, where sharp sounds typically map onto angular shapes and soft sounds onto rounded ones, possibly constitute a peculiar case of such correspondences, as it was documented in preverbal infants and non-human species.
